bib.title: Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 8154-8173

question: Can an LLM reason better if it is repurposed as both a reasoning agent and a world model and searched with Monte Carlo Tree Search, instead of generating one autoregressive chain?
hypothesis: LLMs fail at planning and multi-step reasoning because they lack an internal world model and a reward signal; adding both plus MCTS should improve plan generation, math and logical reasoning.
contributions: RAP framework: the same LLM acts as reasoning agent and world model (state transitions via prompting)
Reward designs (action likelihood, state confidence, self-evaluation, task-specific heuristics) and MCTS planning over reasoning traces
Experiments on Blocksworld, GSM8K and PrOntoQA, with LLaMA-33B beating GPT-4 CoT on Blocksworld

method.summary: A frozen LLM proposes d candidate actions per node and, with a different prompt, predicts the next state; MCTS (selection by UCT, expansion, simulation with a greedy local-reward roll-out, back-propagation) builds a reasoning tree under task-specific rewards. The best-reward path is chosen; for GSM8K multiple paths are aggregated.
method.task: plan generation (Blocksworld), math word problems (GSM8K), logical reasoning (PrOntoQA)

datasets.name: Blocksworld (Valmeekam et al. 2023), subset
datasets.split: test cases grouped by minimum number of actions

datasets.name: Full Blocksworld
datasets.split: Easy: 10 demo cases per step-group, rest test; Hard: 10 random demo cases from the full set excluded from test

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.split: main table: not stated; Table 6 ablation uses first 300 examples

datasets.name: PrOntoQA
datasets.split: sampled from the generation script of Saparov and He (2022); true ontology, random rule ordering, 3/4/5 hops mixed

other.note: default base LLM for RAP and baselines; frozen

inference.decoding: random sampling, generation cut off at max length 2048 or a newline token
inference.samples: Blocksworld: RAP evaluates a single plan; CoT pass@10 uses 10 plans. GSM8K: SC(10) and RAP(10) (10 samples/iterations); PrOntoQA: 20 MCTS iterations vs 20 SC samples. Number of runs/seeds not stated.
inference.prompting: Blocksworld: 4 in-context test cases with solutions (same prompt for CoT and for RAP action likelihood); GSM8K: same 4-shot demos for all methods; Easy/Hard Blocksworld: 4-shot sampled from a 10-case pool; Appendix E adaptive prompting truncates demonstration traces as tree deepens

parameters.mcts_iterations: RAP(10), RAP(20) on Blocksworld; RAP(10) on GSM8K and full Blocksworld; 20 on PrOntoQA
parameters.gsm8k_reward: r = r1^alpha * r2^(1-alpha) (weighted geometric mean of self-evaluation helpfulness and state confidence); alpha value not stated
parameters.state_confidence: multiple sampled answers, proportion of the most frequent answer; number of samples not stated
parameters.q_update_gsm8k_prontoqa: max over future steps of average reward (Eq 2)
parameters.final_path_selection: path from iterations that yielded the highest reward (observed best)
parameters.blocksworld_rewards: r1 action log-likelihood, r2 goal-conditions-met heuristic with a very large reward on full goal

other.simulation: roll-out picks the best local-reward action of d candidates, dropping costly reward parts

metrics.name: Success rate (Blocksworld)
metrics.definition: fraction of test cases with a correct plan; pass@10 solved if any of 10 plans correct

metrics.name: Pred Acc / Proof Acc (PrOntoQA)
metrics.definition: accuracy of the final true/false answer / of the entire proof

eval.protocol: single run per configuration as printed; no seeds, variance or significance tests reported

prompts.text: I am playing with a set of blocks where I need to arrange the blocks into stacks. Here are the actions I can do ... [STATEMENT] As initial conditions I have that, <initial_state> My goal is to have that <goals>. My plan is as follows: [PLAN]
prompts.where: Appendix C.1 (abridged here; full text with 4 demos in paper)

prompts.purpose: Blocksworld world-model state update (per action type)
prompts.text: After being given an initial state and an action, give the new state after performing the action. [SCENARIO 1] [STATE 0] ... [ACTION] ... [CHANGE] ... [STATE 1] ... [SCENARIO 3] [STATE 0] <state> [ACTION] <action> [CHANGE]

prompts.purpose: GSM8K action proposal and next state
prompts.text: Given a question, please decompose it into sub-questions. For each sub-question, please answer it in a complete sentence, ending with "The answer is". When the original question is answerable, please start the subquestion with "Now we can answer the question: ".
Given a list of facts, and a current claim, output one possible fact as the next step. Be sure to copy the exact sentences in the facts. Do not change any wording. Do not create your own words.

evidence.quote: We use random sampling with a temperature of 0.8. The generation is cut off at the maximum length of 2048 or a newline token.

results.claim: RAP with 20 iterations on LLaMA-33B solves 42% of 6-step Blocksworld problems where CoT with LLaMA-33B solves none.
results.setup: Blocksworld 6-step cases, LLaMA-33B, single plan, temperature 0.8, 4-shot

results.claim: RAP(20) solves all 2-step and 88% of 4-step Blocksworld cases.
GPT-4 with CoT scores 0.50/0.63/0.40 on 2/4/6-step Blocksworld; RAP(20) on LLaMA-33B gives 1.00/0.88/0.42.
results.note: Text claims 33% relative gain over GPT-4 in the abstract and Section 4.1; RAP(20) is ahead of GPT-4 CoT in every column of Table 1

results.quote: achieving an average success rate of 64%

results.claim: CoT pass@10 on LLaMA-33B still fails 6-step Blocksworld.
On GSM8K RAP(10) reaches 48.6% against 46.8% for CoT with 10-sample self-consistency.

limits: Authors: only frozen LLMs, abilities bounded by pretraining; fine-tuning as world model and tool use left to future work.
No variance, seeds or significance reported; compute cost (model calls, tokens per question) of MCTS not reported.
Only three task families; hyperparameters d, L, w, alpha not stated in the text.
Reward combination chosen by heuristics and exploratory experiments; effect of rewards depends on the task (action likelihood hurts GSM8K with more iterations).
GSM8K size and split for the main table are not stated; GPT-4 compared only on Blocksworld.

figures.caption: An overview of Reasoning via Planning (RAP). Compared with previous LLM reasoning methods like Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al., 2022), we explicitly model the world state from a world model (repurposed from the language model), and leverage advanced planning algorithms to solve the reasoning problems.
figures.why: Shows the agent/world-model loop versus a plain chain.

figures.caption: An illustration of the four phases in an iteration in MCTS planning (Section 3.3).
figures.why: Selection, expansion, simulation, back-propagation in one picture.

figures.caption: Comparing reasoning traces in Blocksworld from CoT (left) and RAP (right).
figures.why: Shows RAP tracking state and recovering from a wrong first plan.
